From: pharmacovigilance@nordic-pharma.com
To: safety@clinicverse.com
Subject: ICSR - Serious Adverse Event - Stevens-Johnson Syndrome - Celecoxib
Date: 2025-09-08T11:00:00Z

INDIVIDUAL CASE SAFETY REPORT (ICSR)
Initial Report - Serious

Report Reference: AE-2025-4471
Report Date: 2025-09-08
Source: Spontaneous (Healthcare Professional)

=== PATIENT INFORMATION ===
Patient ID: SYN-5578
Age: 72 years
Sex: Female
Weight: 64 kg
Height: 162 cm
Ethnicity: Caucasian

Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (diagnosed 2019)
- Hypertension (controlled with Lisinopril)
- Type 2 Diabetes (managed with Metformin)
- No history of autoimmune disease
- No prior NSAID reactions documented

=== SUSPECT PRODUCT ===
Product: Celebrex (celecoxib) 200mg capsules
Manufacturer: Nordic Pharmaceuticals
Lot Number: NP-CEL-2025-667
NDC: 11111-222-33
Dose: 200mg once daily
Route: Oral
Indication: Osteoarthritis pain
Start Date: 2025-08-25
Stop Date: 2025-09-03 (discontinued due to event)

=== CONCOMITANT MEDICATIONS ===
1. Lisinopril 10mg daily (since 2020)
2. Metformin 500mg BID (since 2018)
3. Calcium carbonate 600mg daily (since 2022)
4. Vitamin D3 1000 IU daily (since 2022)

=== EVENT DESCRIPTION ===
Onset Date: 2025-09-01 (Day 7 of celecoxib therapy)
Location: Patient's home, followed by hospital admission

Clinical Course:
Day 7 (2025-09-01): Patient noticed "sunburn-like" rash on
  trunk. Initially attributed to new laundry detergent.

Day 8 (2025-09-02): Rash spread to arms, legs, and face.
  Developed fever (38.9C / 102F). Oral blisters noted.
  Patient went to Emergency Department.

Day 8 ED Assessment:
  - Vital Signs: T 38.9C, HR 102, BP 118/74, RR 18, SpO2 97%
  - Skin: Erythematous maculopapular rash with targetoid lesions
    covering approximately 35% BSA. Multiple oral erosions on
    buccal mucosa and tongue. Two large blisters on forearms.
  - Eyes: Conjunctival injection, bilateral. No corneal erosions.
  - Nikolsky sign: Positive (skin slippage with gentle pressure)

Day 8 Diagnosis: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS)
  - Severity: SJS (not TEN - BSA involvement <10% with full-thickness)
  - Causality Assessment: Probable (Naranjo score: 8)
  - Suspected trigger: Celecoxib

Day 8-14: Hospital Admission - Burn Unit/ICU
  - Celecoxib discontinued immediately
  - Wound care with silver sulfadiazine dressings
  - IV fluids: Normal saline 125 mL/hr
  - Pain management: Morphine PCA
  - Ophthalmology consult: Artificial tears q2h, no corneal involvement
  - Nutrition: NPO initially, then soft diet when oral lesions improved
  - Infection prevention: Contact precautions, daily wound cultures

Day 10: Skin biopsy results
  - Histopathology: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis with subepidermal
    blister formation. Consistent with SJS.
  - Direct immunofluorescence: Negative

Day 14 (2025-09-08): Discharged to home
  - BSA involvement improved to approximately 10%
  - Oral lesions healing
  - Renal function normal (Cr 0.8 mg/dL)
  - No ocular sequelae

=== OUTCOME ===
Recovering (not yet recovered at time of report)
Expected sequelae: Minor scarring on forearms
Follow-up: Dermatology in 2 weeks, Ophthalmology in 4 weeks

=== SERIOUSNESS CRITERIA ===
[X] Results in hospitalization (prolonged)
[X] Is life-threatening
[X] Other medically important condition

=== CAUSAL ASSESSMENT ===
Reporter Assessment: Probable
Naranjo Score: 8 (Probable)
Rationale:
- Temporal relationship (7 days after initiation)
- Known class effect of COX-2 inhibitors
- Positive dechallenge (improved after discontinuation)
- Alternative causes unlikely (no new medications, no infections)

=== REPORTER INFORMATION ===
Name: Dr. Astrid Lindgren, MD
Specialty: Internal Medicine / Rheumatology
Facility: Nordic Regional Medical Center
Email: a.lindgren@nordic-medical.org
Phone: +46-8-555-0199

=== REGULATORY ===
Reportable to: FDA, EMA, Nordic Regulatory Authority
Patient consent obtained for reporting
